hints: Focus on what each definition actually produces, atoms, ions or electrons, not just what it starts with.
Write the standard equation for first ionisation energy, $\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^+(\text{g}) + \text{e}^-$, and notice a positive ion is clearly formed.
Compare heterolytic fission which splits both electrons to one atom to give a cation and anion, with atomisation which only gives neutral gaseous atoms.
walkthrough:
**Recall first ionisation energy**

Think of knocking the first electron right off a gaseous atom. That must leave a positive ion behind.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^+(\text{g}) + \text{e}^-$$

**Recall heterolytic fission**

Here a covalent bond breaks unevenly. Both shared electrons go to one atom.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{A-B} \rightarrow \text{A}^+ + \text{B}^-$$

**Recall enthalpy change of atomisation**

This is forming one mole of neutral gaseous atoms from the element in its standard state. No electrons are lost and no ions are made.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{Na(s)} \rightarrow \text{Na(g)}$$

**Put it together**

Statements 1 and 2 both include formation of a positive ion, but statement 3 gives only neutral atoms. So 1 and 2 only is the correct combination.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three statements. Statement 3 is atomisation to neutral $\text{X(g)}$, so no positive ion is formed. This is the trap of confusing gaseous atoms with gaseous ions.
options.B: Correct because 1 and 2 only both form a positive ion. First ionisation gives $\text{X}^+(\text{g}) + \text{e}^-$, and heterolytic fission gives a cation plus an anion, for example $\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{H}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$.
options.C: Incorrect because it pairs 2 and 3. While 2 is correct, 3 is wrong since atomisation produces neutral atoms, not ions. It also wrongly leaves out 1, which is the classic example of positive ion formation.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only 1. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct and is missed. Students choose this if they think heterolytic fission only forms free radicals or only forms negative ions.
